children: A DEA judge has paused a hearing regarding the Trump administration's request to move marijuana to a Schedule III drug from a Schedule I drug over a recent Government Accountability Office report that found "gaps" in the federal government's drug scheduling process.
DEA Chief Administrative Law Judge Derek Julius on Tuesday granted a stay on Tuesday to groups who are opposed to the rescheduling,
The groups, who are mostly related to the drug testing industry, want the GAO report entered into the hearing record.
In their request for a stay, the groups argued that GAO's conclusions indicate "the Government therefore lacks written criteria for a finding it must make to move marijuana to Schedule III."

The report, issued Sept. 23, states that the DEA does not have policies that identify roles, responsibilities, and procedures when making scheduling decisions. Also, the FDA doesn't specify how its employees conduct evaluations or develop recommendations.
Julius has asked the DEA to submit a response on whether to add the GAO report to the record by Oct. 13.

title: DEA marijuana rescheduling hearing halted over GAO report
